🇲🇽🏭 US SWALLOWS 76% OF MEXICO'S CAR EXPORTS AS JUNE SHIPMENTS DROP 9.2%

Mexican light-vehicle exports fell 9.2% in June year-on-year, INEGI reported, with the United States absorbing 75.9% of everything Mexico shipped abroad in the first half of 2026 — one buyer taking three-quarters of the market, fully exposed to Trump's tariff swings. The case for trade diversification isn't ideological anymore, it's arithmetic.

🇲🇽📈 MEXICO #2 IN THE OECD FOR REAL WAGE GROWTH — AHEAD OF THE US AND CANADA

Mexican workers' real wages rose 15.1% since 2021 — more than triple the 4.9% OECD average — putting Mexico second among all member states behind only Slovenia, while the US and Canada saw real wages fall, per the OECD. The driver: relentless minimum-wage hikes under AMLO and Sheinbaum that neoliberal economists swore would destroy jobs.

🚨🇲🇽 SUPREME COURT TAKES UP AYOTZINAPA — TRUTH COMMISSION ON THE LINE

Mexico's Supreme Court voted 8-0 to review whether a federal court can order an independent Truth Commission to investigate the 2014 disappearance of the 43 Ayotzinapa students — a commission the FGR has resisted. Twelve years on, the fight over who controls the investigation, and whether victims get a seat at the table, reaches the highest court in the country.

🇲🇽🌎 NO APOLOGY, NO RELATIONS: MEXICO HOLDS THE LINE ON ECUADOR

Sheinbaum reaffirmed Mexico will not restore diplomatic ties with Ecuador until Quito formally apologizes for storming Mexico's embassy and dragging out asylee Jorge Glas by force — a flagrant breach of the Vienna Convention. "Otherwise, it becomes very complex," she said, with Mexico's case against Ecuador still live at the International Court of Justice.

🇲🇽☀️ MEXICO PUTS FREE SOLAR PANELS ON WORKING-CLASS ROOFS

Sheinbaum's "Sol del Norte" program is installing 5,500 rooftop solar panels on Mexicali's most vulnerable homes at zero cost to families — put up in a single day and cutting electricity bills up to 70% in a city of brutal summers. It's a 200-million-peso CFE investment, already expanding to Hermosillo, with 150,000 homes targeted nationwide across the sexenio.

🇲🇽🇨🇺 MEXICO JOINS 136 NATIONS TO FORCE A UN DEBATE ON ENDING THE CUBA BLOCKADE

Mexico voted with 135 other countries — 136 to 9, with 30 abstentions — to open a UN General Assembly debate on ending Washington's 64-year blockade of Cuba, despite Marco Rubio ordering US embassies worldwide to strong-arm host governments into stopping it. Cuba's foreign minister Bruno Rodríguez put the damage from March 2025 to February 2026 alone at $8.1 billion.

🇲🇽🏭 On Toyota: “Trump himself attributes it to his tariffs” "It is not from the annual reviews. Trump himself attributes this decision to the tariffs he imposed on Mexico. What Toyota tells us is that it's part of its global review. And our job is to guarantee jobs and keep the investment coming." — President Claudia Sheinbaum — on Toyota and tariffs Toyota will gradually shift part of its Tacoma production from Tijuana to the US in a process ending in 2030. It keeps its Guanajuato plant (2,800 direct jobs), and Economy confirmed a new auto investment of over $500 million to be announced soon.

🔥🇲🇽 “Who polarizes? Those who spread fake news to sway opinion through lies” "Who polarizes? Those who spread fake news seek to sway opinion through lies — what greater polarization than that?" — President Claudia Sheinbaum — on disinformation Right-wing accounts pushed a false claim that Ecuador's team had been 'threatened by a criminal group' before Mexico beat them at the World Cup; Ecuador itself denied it. Sheinbaum: differences of opinion are democracy — lies are the polarization. She noted the same figures now weaponize the national team against AMLO.

🇲🇽🔍 Sinaloa security report: 2,540 arrests, 5,900 firearms, 2,412 meth labs dismantled "Under President Claudia Sheinbaum's administration, in the state of Sinaloa alone, 2,540 people have been arrested for high-impact crimes." — Security Secretary Omar García Harfuch — Sinaloa report García Harfuch reported the National Security Strategy in Sinaloa: 16,440 troops deployed; 2,540 arrests; over 94.5 tons of drugs and 5,900 firearms seized (about 20% of all weapons seized nationwide this term); and 2,412 clandestine meth labs dismantled. Daily homicide victims are down 44% since June 2025.
